raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Qwen25Detector.parse_streaming_increment` delegates to the base implementation,
which emits at most one unit per increment: a tool name with empty parameters, then
that call's argument diff, then the next call. Whatever a delta leaves pending is
normally picked up by the following delta -- but the detector never overrode
`finish()`, whose documented contract is to release what is still held when the
stream ends, so a delta carrying whole calls loses everything after the first unit.

With four calls in one response, the same input degrades as the delta grows:

```
chunk size  13 -> 4 calls, all arguments present
chunk size  87 -> 3 calls
chunk size 128 -> 3 calls, the last with EMPTY arguments
chunk size 152 -> 2 calls
chunk size 517 -> 1 call with EMPTY arguments      (one delta for the whole response)

detect_and_parse for the same text: 4 calls, all arguments present
```

and for a single call whose whole body lands in the final delta:

```
streamed arguments: ""      <- unusable tool call
expected          : {"city": "NYC", "state": "NY", "unit": "celsius"}
```

This is reachable whenever a call completes inside one delta -- multi-token deltas
from speculative decoding / MTP, `stream_interval > 1`, or a call short enough to
be generated in one step -- and it is worse than a display bug: the client receives
a tool call it cannot dispatch, or never learns about calls the model made.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen25_detector.py` (+39):

- `finish()` re-runs the parser with an empty delta until a round yields neither
  calls nor text, releasing the pending queue. This follows the pattern
  `GigaChat35Detector.finish()` already uses.
- Text the detector held back because a partial end token could still arrive is
  released as well: the stream is over, so it never will. `</tool_call>` is
  stripped from it, since that token is framing rather than content.

`test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py` (+91): three
cases in `TestQwen25Detector`, parametrized over the chunk sizes above; two of them
fail on `main`.

## Scope: what this deliberately does not change

- **Text preceding a call is still dropped when the call shares its delta** (for the
  single-call example above, at 48 characters per delta the client sees no prose).
  That happens inside the shared `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment`
  path, which stops emitting text as soon as the buffer contains a marker, so it
  affects every detector that delegates there rather than being a Qwen-specific
  bug. #35625 targets that shared path and should own it.
- The non-streaming path numbers every call `tool_index = 0`; streaming numbers
  them 0, 1, 2, 3. That asymmetry is not part of this fix and the regression tests
  compare `(name, arguments)` so they do not depend on it either way.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A -- parser-only change, no model forward or kernel code touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A -- the added work is bounded by the number of pending units at the end of a
stream.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; the detector
      has zero findings and the test file keeps its 6 pre-existing `F841`.
- [x] Add unit tests per the repo's admission criteria (bug regression: the two
      behaviour cases fail before the change and pass after it).
- [x] Duplicate pre-check: searched open PRs on
      `python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen25_detector.py` -- none.
- [ ] Documentation: N/A

### Verification

```
pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py
# 253 passed, 51 subtests passed          (250 before this change)

pytest ... -k "releases_all_calls_at_end_of_stream or releases_arguments_... or noop_when_nothing"
# with the fix:      3 passed
# detector reverted: 2 failed, 1 passed

pytest test/registered/unit/function_call test/registered/unit/parser
# 1064 passed, 1793 subtests passed
```

---

Disclosure: prepared with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness). The reproduction, the
pre-fix failures and the post-fix passes were all executed locally on CPU with
`PYTHONPATH` pointed at the checkout.

**Reviewer note — why the drain sits in `finish()` and not in the base class.**

There is an open base-class fix for part of this defect class (#32167, "Fix streaming tool calls losing arguments when completed in the final delta"). It does not cover this detector, and the reason is worth recording before anyone has to ask:

- The shared flush path is `FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_end()` -> `detector.finish()`, and **both** streaming entrypoints call it (`serving_chat.py:3030`, `serving_responses.py:2399`). The flush that #32167 extends, `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args`, exists only in `serving_chat.py` (defined at 3115, used at 945); `serving_responses.py` has no equivalent.
- `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` processes exactly **one** JSON object per call — there is no loop between the `bot_token` search and the Case 1 / Case 2 returns. A delta carrying several complete calls therefore leaves the rest buffered, and registering the single object that was parsed does not recover them; the drain here re-runs the parser until it yields nothing, which does.
- `Qwen25Detector.parse_streaming_increment` calls `super().parse_streaming_increment(...)` and then post-processes the result, so the parse is shared but the one-unit-per-increment limit is not lifted: the four-calls-in-one-delta case in the description still needs the drain.

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Searched open PRs by file path, class name and defect description. `#32167` ("Fix
streaming tool calls losing arguments when completed in the final delta") is the closest
base-class competitor; the reasoning why this detector-level fix is not subsumed by it is
in the reviewer note above. No other open PR fixes the one-unit-per-increment drain for
`Qwen25Detector`.

files.patch:
@@ -8,11 +8,16 @@
 from sglang.srt.function_call.core_types import (
     StreamingParseResult,
     StructureInfo,
+    ToolCallItem,
     _GetInfoFunc,
 )
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+# Upper bound for the end-of-stream drain: each round releases at most one
+# pending unit (a tool name or one argument diff).
+_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS = 1024
+
 
 class Qwen25Detector(BaseFormatDetector):
     """
@@ -112,6 +117,38 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
 
         return result
 
+    def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:
+        """Release state the last delta left pending.
+
+        The base implementation emits the tool name first and its arguments on a
+        later call, so a delta carrying a complete call leaves the arguments
+        pending -- and when that delta was the last one (multi-token deltas from
+        speculative decoding / MTP, ``stream_interval > 1``, or a short call
+        generated in one step) the call reached the client with empty arguments,
+        or later calls were dropped entirely, while detect_and_parse returned
+        them in full.
+
+        Re-running the parser with an empty delta drains that queue. Text the
+        detector held back because a partial end token could still arrive is
+        released too: the stream is over, so it never will.
+        """
+        normal_parts: List[str] = []
+        calls: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        for _ in range(_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS):
+            result = self.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+            if not result.calls and not result.normal_text:
+                break
+            if result.calls:
+                calls.extend(result.calls)
+
+        if self._normal_text_buffer:
+            pending, self._normal_text_buffer = self._normal_text_buffer, ""
+            pending = pending.replace(self.eot_token[1:], "")
+            if pending:
+                normal_parts.append(pending)
+
+        return StreamingParseResult(normal_text="".join(normal_parts), calls=calls)
+
     def structure_info(self) -> _GetInfoFunc:
         return lambda name: StructureInfo(
             begin='<tool_call>\n{"name":"' + name + '", "arguments":',

@@ -37,6 +37,7 @@
 from sglang.srt.function_call.parser_names import TOOL_CALL_PARSER_NAMES
 from sglang.srt.function_call.pythonic_detector import PythonicDetector
 from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen3_coder_detector import Qwen3CoderDetector
+from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen25_detector import Qwen25Detector
 from sglang.srt.function_call.utils import get_schema_properties
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
 
@@ -5507,6 +5508,119 @@ def test_streaming_multiple_tool_calls_char_by_char_separator(self):
         cities = [json.loads(result[i]["parameters"])["city"] for i in sorted(result)]
         self.assertEqual(cities, ["NYC", "LA"])
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _collect_qwen25(chunks, tools):
+        """Feed deltas and merge streamed calls the way a client would."""
+        detector = Qwen25Detector()
+        calls: list = []
+        text = ""
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools)
+            text += result.normal_text or ""
+            calls.extend(result.calls)
+        end = detector.finish(tools)
+        text += end.normal_text or ""
+        calls.extend(end.calls)
+        # merge argument deltas per tool index, then drop the index: the
+        # non-streaming path numbers every call 0, which is not the contract here
+        merged: dict = {}
+        order = []
+        for call in calls:
+            if call.tool_index not in merged:
+                merged[call.tool_index] = [call.name, ""]
+                order.append(call.tool_index)
+            if call.name:
+                merged[call.tool_index][0] = call.name
+            merged[call.tool_index][1] += call.parameters or ""
+        return text, [(merged[i][0], merged[i][1]) for i in order]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _non_stream_calls(text, tools):
+        result = Qwen25Detector().detect_and_parse(text, tools)
+        return [(c.name, c.parameters) for c in result.calls]
+
+    PARALLEL_OUTPUT = (
+        '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+        '{"city": "NYC", "state": "NY", "unit": "fahrenheit"}}\n</tool_call>\n'
+        '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+        '{"city": "Baltimore", "state": "MD", "unit": "fahrenheit"}}\n</tool_call>\n'
+        '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+        '{"city": "Minneapolis", "state": "MN", "unit": "fahrenheit"}}\n</tool_call>\n'
+        '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+        '{"city": "Los Angeles", "state": "CA", "unit": "fahrenheit"}}\n</tool_call>'
+    )
+
+    def test_finish_releases_all_calls_at_end_of_stream(self):
+        """Every call must survive any framing, including one delta per response.
+
+        The parser emits one unit per increment, so a delta carrying whole calls
+        leaves the rest pending; with no finish() override and a delta large
+        enough to hold several calls, later calls and their arguments were
+        dropped -- four calls became two, then one with empty arguments.
+        """
+        tools = self.tools
+        expected = self._non_stream_calls(self.PARALLEL_OUTPUT, tools)
+        self.assertEqual(len(expected), 4)
+
+        for chunk_size in (13, 87, 128, 152, 200, len(self.PARALLEL_OUTPUT)):
+            text = self.PARALLEL_OUTPUT
+            chunks = [text[i : i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(text), chunk_size)]
+            _, streamed = self._collect_qwen25(chunks, tools)
+            self.assertEqual(streamed, expected, f"chunk_size={chunk_size}")
+
+    def test_finish_releases_arguments_of_a_call_completed_in_one_delta(self):
+        """A call completing inside one delta must not arrive with empty args."""
+        text = (
+            "Sure, let me check the weather.\n"
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+            '{"city": "NYC", "state": "NY", "unit": "celsius"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+        tools = self.tools
+        expected = self._non_stream_calls(text, tools)
+        for chunk_size in (24, 48, 100, len(text)):
+            chunks = [text[i : i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(text), chunk_size)]
+            _, streamed = self._collect_qwen25(chunks, tools)
+            self.assertEqual(streamed, expected, f"chunk_size={chunk_size}")
+            for _, parameters in streamed:
+                json.loads(parameters)
+
+    def test_finish_is_a_noop_when_nothing_is_pending(self):
+        text = (
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": '
+            '{"city": "NYC", "state": "NY", "unit": "celsius"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+        tools = self.tools
+        detector = Qwen25Detector()
+        detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, tools)
+        detector.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+
+        end = detector.finish(tools)
+        self.assertEqual(end.calls, [])
+        self.assertEqual(end.normal_text, "")
+
+    def test_finish_releases_text_withheld_for_a_partial_end_token(self):
+        """Text held back for a partial end token must not be dropped at stream end.
+
+        The streaming path keeps a trailing prefix of ``</tool_call>`` in
+        ``_normal_text_buffer`` in case the rest of the token arrives. When the
+        stream ends that token never will, so the text has to be released:
+        ``detect_and_parse`` returns those same bytes as normal text.
+        """
+        text = "Hello</tool"
+        detector = Qwen25Detector()
+        chunk = detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, self.tools)
+        end = detector.finish(self.tools)
+
+        # "Hello" streams, the partial token is withheld, and finish() releases it.
+        self.assertEqual(chunk.normal_text, "Hello")
+        self.assertEqual(end.normal_text, "</tool")
+
+        expected = Qwen25Detector().detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (chunk.normal_text or "") + (end.normal_text or ""),
+            (expected.normal_text or "").strip(),
+        )
+
 
 class TestGemma4Detector(unittest.TestCase):
     def setUp(self):
